about: Clearance holes and screw head recesses for ISO metric screws, for the Hole feature's Clearance holes (mitcad#903), and nut pockets and heat-set insert holes for printed parts (mitcad#1518). Mitcad's own data (MIT licence): the dimensions tabulated from the standards each section names, in millimetres and degrees. The sizes are those of MitCad's fastener tables (tools/libraries/make-fastener-library.py), M1.6 to M24; a section without a size has no row for it. The commands store the values the panel fills in as plain values: this table is only where they come from.

iso_273.title: ISO 273 (ISO 20273): clearance holes for bolts and screws
iso_273.about: The clearance hole diameter dh of the fine, medium and coarse series for the nominal thread diameter d. The Hole panel's Fit Normal is the medium series.

din_974_1.title: DIN 974-1, series 1: counterbores for hexagon socket head cap screws (ISO 4762) without washers
din_974_1.about: The counterbore diameter d1 of series 1. The depth is the head height k (max) of ISO 4762 plus an allowance that puts the head below the face: 0.2 mm for M1.6 to M2.5, 0.4 mm for M3 to M6, 0.6 mm for M8 to M20 and 0.8 mm for M24 (M6: 6 + 0.4 = 6.4). A counterdrill takes the same diameter and depth.

iso_10642.title: ISO 10642: hexagon socket countersunk head screws, 90 degrees
iso_10642.about: The head's theoretical diameter dk (max), where its 90-degree cone meets its top: a countersink of this diameter puts the top of the head at the face. The standard has M3 to M20.

iso_15065.title: ISO 15065: countersinks for countersunk head screws with heads of ISO 7721
iso_15065.about: The countersink diameter d2 (min) at 90 degrees for the heads of ISO 7721 (the screws of ISO 2009, ISO 7046 and others); the standard has the sizes up to M10.

countersink.about: A clearance hole's countersink: 90 degrees, its diameter the larger of ISO 10642's head diameter and ISO 15065's countersink, so that the head of either screw is at or just below the face; a size neither standard has (M24) has none.

tapped_countersink.about: A tapped hole's countersink: just over the thread's major diameter, factor times it rounded to 0.1 mm (at least 0.1 mm over it), at 90 degrees, so that the first thread does not raise a burr.

iso_4032.title: ISO 4032: hexagon regular nuts (style 1)
iso_4032.about: The nut's width across flats s and its height m (max) for the nominal thread diameter d, the same values as MitCad's nut library (tools/libraries/make-fastener-library.py). A nut pocket (mitcad#1518) is the nut with the clearance of nut_pocket.

nut_pocket.about: A printed part's hex pocket for an ISO 4032 nut (mitcad#1518): the nut's width across flats plus the clearance, and its height plus the clearance as the pocket's depth (M3: 5.5 + 0.3 = 5.8 across the flats, 2.4 + 0.3 = 2.7 deep). The clearance is MitCad's own default for printed pockets, which the hole_sizes query's nut_clearance replaces.

heat_set_insert.title: Heat-set threaded inserts for printed parts: ruthex's published hole diameters and insert lengths
heat_set_insert.about: The hole for a heat-set threaded insert (mitcad#1518): the hole diameter is the drill size ruthex publishes for its threaded inserts of each thread size (its drill bit set for threaded inserts: M2 3.2 mm, M2.5 and M3 4 mm, M4 5.6 mm, M5 6.4 mm, M6 8 mm), the length that of its standard insert of the size (RX-M2x4, RX-M2.5x5.7, RX-M3x5.7, RX-M4x8.1, RX-M5x9.5, RX-M6x12.7). The hole's depth is the insert's length plus MitCad's own allowance of 1 mm, room for the plastic the insert displaces. The diameters and lengths are dimensions of commercial products, facts tabulated here as MitCad's own data (MIT licence); no text or drawing of the source is copied. The other sizes have no insert in the series.
